title: Mountain Climber: How to Do It Correctly at Home
intro: The mountain climber is an exercise done from a plank position while bringing your knees to your chest, one at a time. It trains your abs and raises your heart rate at the same time.
muscles: Abs and core, shoulders, chest, thighs and glutes. It also trains your heart stamina.
steps: Start in a straight-arm plank, hands under your shoulders.
Keep your body straight from head to heels, tummy tight.
Bring your right knee towards your chest, then return.
Bring your left knee towards your chest, then return.
Keep alternating at a controlled pace.
mistakes: Hips lifted too high. Keep your hips roughly level with your shoulders.
Lower back sagging. Tighten your tummy like you're bracing for a punch.
Hands too far forward. Place your hands directly under your shoulders so your shoulders aren't overloaded.
easier: Put your hands on a sturdy sofa, table or stair step so your body is more upright, and do it slowly as a stepping movement.
harder: Go faster, or bring your knee towards the opposite elbow (cross-body mountain climber).
dose: Beginner: 3 sets x 20 seconds, rest 40 seconds. Do it 2-3 times a week.
safety: Stop if you feel pain in your wrists, shoulders or lower back. If the pain continues, or you have just given birth or have back problems, see a doctor or physio first.

faq.q: My wrists hurt during the plank. Why?
faq.a: This is common for beginners. Try the hands-on-sofa or table version, spread your fingers, and press into the floor with your whole palm.

faq.q: Can mountain climbers flatten my tummy?
faq.a: They strengthen your abs, but they can't burn fat from your tummy only. Tummy fat goes down when your eating and overall movement are consistent.

faq.q: Do I need to go fast?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Go slow with good form first. You can add speed once you're stable.
